title: Open Homepage
rationale: Opening the root URL must render the default homepage. The global navigation is present on the homepage, so asserting the visible Shelves and Books navigation links confirms the homepage is displayed.

title: Back to Homepage from Other Pages
rationale: To start from a non-homepage page, open the shelf list via the visible Shelves navigation link and confirm the list is displayed using the seeded shelf. Clicking the BookStack logo should return to the homepage, confirmed by the reappearance of the global navigation links.

title: Enter Login Page
rationale: From a fresh browser context, open the homepage and click the Login link in the global navigation. The login page should appear with email and password fields. No seed state is required beyond the default unauthenticated session.

title: Log In Successfully
rationale: From a fresh context, navigate to the login page via the homepage login link. Fill in the verified account credentials from the contract (bookstack_user@example.com / Password123!), enable Remember Me, and submit. The authenticated homepage should appear and display the user's nickname 'BookStack User' in the top-right area.

title: Enter Authenticated Homepage
rationale: This scenario requires the user to be authenticated, so the given steps log in with the verified seeded account. After login the natural post-login navigation should land on the homepage dashboard, where the four overview sections are expected to be visible as headings.

title: View Shelf List
rationale: Open the application entry to see the global navigation bar. Click the Shelves navigation link to open the shelf list page; the seeded shelf 'Shelf 4.1' appears on the list, proving the shelf list is displayed. Authentication is not needed because REQ-4 depends only on REQ-1.1, not REQ-2.

title: Enter Shelf Details Page
rationale: REQ-4.2.1 requires opening the details page of a shelf from the shelf list. The provided seed 'shelf-4-2-1' supplies the shelf named 'Shelf 4.2.1'. The navigation contract from the requirements tree gives the route: open homepage -> click 'Shelves' in the global navigation bar -> click the 'Shelf 4.2.1' item in the shelf list. Authentication is not required for this branch because REQ-4.1 depends only on REQ-1.1.

title: Create Shelf
rationale: Creates a new shelf from an existing shelf's action panel. Preparation logs in if the Login control is visible, navigates through the global navigation to the seeded shelf details, opens the New Shelf form, binds a unique shelf name, fills the required Name field, saves, and then navigates to the shelf list to confirm the new shelf is displayed.

given.source: Unique scenario-derived name that avoids collision with the seeded exact shelf names.

title: Cancel Creation
rationale: Exits the shelf creation flow without saving. Preparation logs in if the Login control is visible, navigates to the seeded shelf details, opens the New Shelf form, binds and fills a unique name so that a failed cancel would be detectable, then clicks Cancel and verifies the shelf list still shows the existing shelf and does not show the new name.

given.source: Unique scenario-derived name used to prove the cancelled creation was not persisted.

title: Confirm Delete Shelf
rationale: Uses the seeded deletable shelf 'Shelf 4.4.1'. From a fresh browser context, open the homepage, navigate via the global Shelves link to the shelf list, open Shelf 4.4.1 details, then use Delete and Confirm to perform the deletion. The subsequent absence of the shelf while another seeded shelf is visible confirms the shelf list is shown and the shelf was removed.

title: Cancel Delete Shelf
rationale: Uses the seeded deletable shelf 'Shelf 4.4.2'. From a fresh browser context, open the homepage, navigate to the shelf list, open Shelf 4.4.2 details, and proceed to the delete confirmation page. Clicking Cancel should return to the shelf details page without deleting, leaving the shelf name visible and the confirmation action absent.

title: Save Shelf Edits
rationale: Editing a shelf requires an authenticated shelf-details context. The seed shelf 'Shelf 4.5.1' is opened through the global Shelves link and the shelf details action panel; after opening the edit form a unique description is entered and saved. The check confirms the redirect back to the shelf details page by asserting the saved description is visible and the edit form save action is no longer present.

when.source: Scenario-specific text used as the new shelf description; it is a valid plain-text value.

title: Cancel Shelf Edits
rationale: The seeded shelf 'Shelf 4.5.2' is opened through the global Shelves link and its edit form is reached via the shelf details action panel. Cancelling the edit form should return to the shelf details page without applying changes, so the original description and the details-page edit action are asserted while the save form action is absent.

title: View Books List
rationale: Open the homepage to show the global navigation bar, then click the Books link to navigate to the books list page. The seeded book 'Book 5.1' should appear as a card, and the 'Create New Book' button confirms the action panel is present.

title: Enter Book Details Page through Book List Page
rationale: Open the application, use the global navigation bar to reach the books list, and click the seeded book card. The route is inferred from the navigation table: Book list -> book card -> book details. Assertions confirm the clicked book name and details-page controls are visible.

title: Enter Book Details Page through Shelf Details Page
rationale: Open the application, use the global navigation bar to reach the shelves list, and open the seeded shelf that contains the seeded book. The route follows the navigation table: Shelves -> shelf item -> book item on shelf details -> book details. Assertions confirm the book name and a details-page control are visible.

title: Fill out and Save Book
rationale: Creation requires an authenticated session based on the user seed (REQ-2.2). Starting from a fresh context, log in, open the Books list from the global navigation, open the create-book form, fill a unique generated name, and save; the resulting book details page is verified by the book name being visible.

given.source: Unique scenario-derived book name; not present in any seed so it can be uniquely asserted after creation.

title: Cancel Creating Book
rationale: The cancel flow requires reaching the create-new-book page. After logging in and opening the Books list, the form is opened and a unique name is entered so cancellation can be proven by the book not appearing afterwards; clicking Cancel should return to the books list with no new book created.

given.source: Unique scenario-derived book name; not present in any seed so absence after cancellation proves no book was created.

title: Save Book Edits
rationale: Seed provides editable book Book 5.4.1 with initial description and tags. Editing requires an authenticated session and the action panel is available to the logged-in user, so log in with the verified seed account, then navigate via Books to Book 5.4.1. Open the edit form, change the name to a unique generated value, and save. The returned details page showing the updated name proves the edit was persisted and the user returned to the details page. UI routes follow the contract navigation entries.

when.source: Unique scenario-derived name; avoids collisions and provides a visible value that can confirm the saved edit on the details page.

title: Cancel Book Edits
rationale: Seed provides editable book Book 5.4.2 with valid initial description and tags. Authenticate as the seed user and navigate to Book 5.4.2 details, then open Edit to reach the edit page. Modify the name field to a generated value and click Cancel; because nothing is saved, the returned details page must still show the original name and must not contain the cancelled name. This verifies the cancel flow returns to details without applying edits.

when.source: Unique generated name used only to demonstrate that cancelling discards edits; it must not appear after returning to the details page.

title: Confirm Delete Book
rationale: This check verifies the book deletion flow. Since deleting a book requires an authenticated session and the action panel, the given phase logs in with the seeded BookStack user, navigates to the books list via the global Books link, opens the seeded deletable book 'Book 5.5.1', and clicks Delete to reach the confirmation page. The when phase confirms the deletion. The then phase asserts that the book is removed from the list and the books list page is shown.

title: Cancel Delete Book
rationale: This check verifies that cancelling the book deletion keeps the book intact. The given phase logs in with the seeded BookStack user, navigates to the books list, opens the seeded book 'Book 5.5.2', and clicks Delete to reach the delete confirmation page. The when phase clicks Cancel. The then phase confirms the user returns to the book details page with the book still present, and then verifies the book remains in the books list.

title: Fill out and Save Book with Shelf
rationale: The scenario creates a new book from the shelf details page via the action panel. Preparation requires authenticating with the seeded user to access creation actions, then navigating to the shelf details for the seeded 'Shelf 5.6.1'. The create flow uses the 'Create New Book' button, fills the required name field, and saves. Verification checks the created book name appears on its details page and also on the shelf details page to confirm association.

when.source: Unique scenario-derived book name to avoid collision with existing book seeds.

title: Save Page
rationale: Prepares authenticated session, navigates to seeded Book 6.1.1, opens the New Page flow, creates a page with a unique name, saves it, and verifies the page appears on the returned book details page. No other scenario data is used.

when.source: Unique scenario-derived name to avoid collisions across parallel workers.

title: Save Draft
rationale: Authenticates, navigates to seeded Book 6.1.2, enters the New Page flow, fills and saves a draft, then returns home and confirms the draft appears under My Recent Drafts. Relies only on seeds for Book 6.1.2 and the shared user.

when.source: Unique scenario-derived name to avoid collisions across parallel workers.

title: Delete Draft
rationale: Authenticates, navigates to seeded Book 6.1.3 which contains draft Draft 6.1.3, opens the draft and, if needed, clicks Edit to reach the page edit screen, deletes and confirms draft deletion, then verifies the draft is removed from the book details page. Uses only seeds for Book 6.1.3, Draft 6.1.3, and the shared user.

title: Create Chapter
rationale: The seeded server contains Book 6.2.1. Because chapter creation requires an authenticated session, the shared BookStack User is logged in through the visible login flow. The user then navigates via the global Books nav to the book details page, opens New Chapter, fills the required name with a unique scenario-derived value, saves, and asserts the new chapter name is visible, confirming the chapter was created for the current book.

when.source: Unique scenario-derived chapter name avoids collisions with any existing chapters and is a valid chapter name.

title: Enter Page Reading Page
rationale: Seeded book 'Book 6.3.1' contains readable page 'Page 6.3.1'. Preparation logs in with the seed account, uses the Books navigation link to reach the book list, opens the seeded book, and then clicks the page entry. Route is inferred from the navigation contract: homepage -> Login -> Books -> book card -> page entry.

title: Redirect to Page Edit Page
rationale: Seeded book 'Book 6.3.2' contains editable page 'Page 6.3.2'. Preparation logs in with the seed account, navigates through Books and Book 6.3.2 to the page reading page, then clicks the Edit action. The resulting edit form should contain the page name. Route is inferred from the navigation contract: homepage -> Login -> Books -> book card -> page entry -> Edit.

title: Add to Recently Viewed
rationale: Verify that opening a shelf details page records it in My Recently Viewed on the authenticated homepage. Seed Shelf 7.1 is provided; use the global nav to navigate to shelves, open the seeded shelf, then return to the homepage and assert the item appears. Preparation requires login with the seeded account since recently-viewed is user-specific and dashboard-only. The UI route is: open homepage -> Login -> Shelves (global nav) -> Shelf 7.1 -> BookStack logo (homepage). No APIs or URLs beyond the entry page are used.

given.source: Seed user from REQ-2.2 provides this verified email.

title: Quick Navigation from Recently Viewed
rationale: Verify that clicking a shelf listed under My Recently Viewed navigates to that shelf's details page. The seeded shelf Shelf 7.2 is used. Because recently-viewed entries only appear after viewing the item in the same authenticated session, this scenario must first open Shelf 7.2, which records it, then return to the homepage and click the entry. Preparation: login with seeded account to make dashboard lists visible. Route: homepage -> Login -> Shelves -> Shelf 7.2 -> BookStack logo -> click My Recently Viewed item.

given.source: Seed user from REQ-2.2 provides the verified login email.

title: Favorite Items
rationale: Favorites require an authenticated session, so prepare by logging in with the seeded user. Navigate to the seeded Book 8.1 via the Books list, then use the Favorite action on the book details page. Verify the action toggles to Unfavorite and that the book appears in the My Most Viewed Favorites dashboard section after returning home.

title: Quick Navigation from Favorites
rationale: To provide the seeded Book 8.2 as a favorite item on the dashboard, log in, open Book 8.2 from the books list, and favorite it. Return to the homepage, click its entry under My Most Viewed Favorites, and confirm the application navigates to the book's details page by checking the page contains the book title and the favorite state button.

title: Quick Navigation from Recently Updated
rationale: The scenario requires the authenticated homepage to show a recently updated page, then navigating to that page's reading view via the Recently Updated Pages list. Because no page seed exists for Book 9.1, the check prepares state by logging in with the declared verified account, opening Book 9.1, creating a uniquely named page, and returning to the homepage so the newly saved page appears in the Recently Updated Pages dashboard section. Navigation from the homepage to the selected page is verified by observing the page title and content on the reading page.

given.source: Unique page name derived from the scenario to avoid colliding with other created pages.
